message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has a GPU attached and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
I’ll give you both:

| What you’ll see | Why it matters |
|-----------------|----------------|
| `gcloud` CLI command | Quick, one‑liner for developers who already have the SDK installed |
| REST‑API `curl` snippet | Useful if you’re building your own automation or want to embed the call in a script that talks directly to the API |
| Notes on GPU availability | The RTX A6000 isn’t offered on GCP – I’ll explain what you can use instead |

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI – the easiest way

```bash
# 1️⃣  Make sure you’re authenticated and have billing enabled
gcloud auth login
gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID
gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-instance \
    --zone us-central1-a \
    --machine-type n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
    --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-v100,count=1 \   # GPU type & count
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 50GB \
    --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \
    --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \
    --restart-on-failure
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | Where the VM lives (pick a zone that supports GPUs) |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM profile |
| `--accelerator` | Attach a GPU (`nvidia-tesla-v100` is the closest to an RTX A6000 that GCP offers) |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size/type` | SSD boot disk, 50 GB |
| `--maintenance-policy` | How to handle zone maintenance (TERMINATE is safe for GPU workloads) |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts if the VM crashes |

> **⚠️ GPU Availability**  
> GCP currently offers NVIDIA Tesla GPUs (T4, P4, V100, A100, etc.). The RTX A6000 is a workstation GPU sold by NVIDIA, not a product GCP sells. If you specifically need an RTX A6000, you’d have to bring your own hardware or use a different provider that offers that GPU.

---

## 2️⃣  REST‑API call (via `curl`)

If you prefer to talk directly to the Compute Engine API, here’s a minimal `curl` example.  
You’ll need an OAuth 2.0 access token with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.

```bash
PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="my-rtx-instance"

# 1️⃣  Get an access token (replace with your method)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# 2️⃣  Build the JSON payload
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/types/nvidia-tesla-v100"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  }
}
EOF

# 3️⃣  POST the request
curl -X POST "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

### Things to keep in mind

* **Authentication** – The `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` command is just one way to get a token. In production you’d probably use a service account key and `gcloud auth activate-service-account`.
* **Zone selection** – Not all zones support GPUs. Use `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="zone:$ZONE"` to confirm.
* **Billing** – The project must have billing enabled; otherwise the API call will fail.

---

## 3️⃣  Quick sanity check

After running either the CLI or the REST call, verify the instance exists:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe my-rtx-instance --zone us-central1-a
```

Look for the `accelerators` section to confirm the GPU was attached:

```json
"accelerators": [
  {
    "acceleratorCount": 1,
    "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/types/nvidia-tesla-v100"
  }
]
```

---

### TL;DR

* **Use `gcloud compute instances create …`** – fastest, no code required.  
* **Or use the REST API** – great for automation or embedding in your own tooling.  
* **GPU type** – GCP offers Tesla GPUs; the RTX A6000 isn’t available. Use `nvidia-tesla-v100` (or another Tesla model) instead.

Happy computing! 🚀
